method: Inspect every assembled 4x image and both complete comparison sheets; retain all raw model outputs locally.

semantics.HOLD: Diamond unit enclosed by unbroken boundary.
semantics.FALL BACK: Diamond unit moves left toward the boundary.
semantics.FOCUS FIRE: Three tips converge on one diamond target.
semantics.UNLEASH: Two tips point outward through split containment.
semantics.ECLIPSE: Occluded disc/crescent for the existing Bloodridge acquired order.

observations: FLUX B housings are darker, quieter and give the pale rune clearer priority; F08 and F09 are the strongest readability candidates so far.
FLUX A is coherent but more conventional fantasy framing, especially F05. These remain alternatives for owner comparison, not equally strong recommendations.

Qwen uses larger fractured and segmented planes. Nine outputs produced unwanted external light markers or beams; bounded cleanup recorded in review_corrections.py removed them before upload. Q10 needed no exterior cleanup.
Q06 and Q08 are the clearest Qwen candidates for restrained dark housings. Q09 has stronger faceting but more edge detail competing with the rune. Q02 and Q05 are more stone-like than neural.
The glyph layer is authored and fixed. The housing comes from each local model generation; these are hybrid candidates rather than raw model outputs.

Pixel processing reduces each housing to 128x128 and the shared 25-colour study palette, including black silhouette outlines. Fine hand cleanup and in-game scale review are still separate from these concepts.
failed_attempts: Initial dual-reference FLUX plus fully remapped modulation LoRA produced all-over texture, not a housing. Rejected and preserved under rejected-dual-reference.
Two dynamic-VRAM jobs stalled at initialization and were stopped without an output. Only this task's jobs were affected.
The final FLUX route uses the previously successful original LoRA: 63 patches load, six key entries are skipped. The attempted compatibility copy is not the final route.
limitations: No blind recognition test, owner approval of the new glyph system, button-state expansion or in-battle readability test.
No Unity, production asset, gameplay-state, save, commit or push changes. No paid API generation.
Some housings are still conventional frame shapes; this is a bounded comparison of alternatives, not a claim that all 20 resolve the cult identity equally well.
